author: @JSchanzer
title: The War Inside the War - Commentary Magazine
text:
The Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, thrust Israel into wars on seven fronts. A new book by Yonah Jeremy Bob, of the Jerusalem Post, and Elliot Kaufman, of the Wall Street Journal, chronicles an eighth front: the battle inside Israel’s war cabinet. In the War Room details the clashes between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Minister without Portfolio Benny Gantz, and Minister of Defense Yoav Gallant. We’ve heard about these conflicts in bits and pieces over the past three years, but until the release of this new book, they lacked a cohesive narrative.
Bob and Kaufman weave the compelling story of Israel’s remarkable achievements on the battlefield against the Iranian regime and its terror proxies together with the utter dysfunction of a war cabinet comprising three politicians. Each had his own aspirations for power, and each had his own distinct understanding of what victory would mean in what is undeniably Israel’s longest and most complex war in the country’s history.
Individually and together, the authors enjoyed remarkable access to the key players involved. Bob embedded with the IDF to visit the tunnels of Gaza and spoke with top officials and their deputies throughout the war. Kaufman interviewed top players in both Israel and America as the war dragged on. The result is the most compelling long-form narrative of Israel’s war to date.
The book reveals the chaos during the early hours of the war. Netanyahu was not awakened until 6:29 that morning, even as Hamas fighters were gunning down Israeli citizens across large swaths of the country’s south. Shockingly, Netanyahu and IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi didn’t speak to each other until the fighting had gone on for four hours.
Bob and Kaufman also detail the dynamic in the U.S.-Israel relationship, including the surprising alliance between Netanyahu and U.S. President Joe Biden early in the war as both men worked to keep the war from widening to involve Hezbollah in Lebanon. This meeting of Machiavellian minds did not last long, as Netanyahu ultimately embraced a more aggressive posture. This put him at odds with Biden and his lieutenants and ultimately led to the (then) unthinkable: America withholding armaments from Israel.
In the War Room also provides glimpses of Hamas’s depravity. The Palestinian terrorist group scuttled three prior mass invasion plans in April 2022, October 2022, and April 2023. But it was only on October 7, 2023, that the group finally unleashed a force of around 5,600 at 119 different locations. The fact that Hamas operated out of tunnels beneath hospitals and schools is, by now, well known. The group invested hundreds of millions of dollars in a subterranean paramilitary maze instead of alleviating the economic challenges faced by some 2 million Gazans. But the authors reveal that Hamas also fought from a large tunnel beneath a cemetery in the heart of Khan Younis.
The unspeakable evil didn’t end there. Months into the war, as negative public sentiment over the death toll of the war continued to mount, with an estimated 30,000 killed, Hamas officials sought to double down. “We have the Israelis right where we want them,” read one Hamas leader’s message reviewed by Kaufman and the Wall Street Journal.
The war with Hezbollah, including the “Grim Beeper” operation and the air strikes that killed longtime leader Hassan Nasrallah a year after the Hamas invasion, is described in terrific detail. The authors reveal that Hezbollah nearly discovered the explosives in their beepers at “earlier times.” And they ask a compelling question about whether “Israel might have saved itself more than a year of war in the north” had the beeper op been executed in the early days after October 7, as Defense Minister Gallant had suggested. Predictably, a “battle over credit” among the war-room principals erupted over these major battlefield achievements.
The Iranian regime’s decision to attack Israel on April 13, 2024, was “the second-largest miss of the war” for Israeli intelligence, the authors claim. Israeli brass simply didn’t believe that the mullahs would make such a move following Israel’s strike on an Iranian outpost in Syria. The episode only reinforces a profound truism of war, namely, that wars produce only one thing consistently: unintended consequences.
________
